name: annotepage-mcp

tools.name: annotepage_open_notes
tools.description:
The review remarks THAT ARE STILL TO BE FIXED, with their reply threads. This is the starting point: an open note points at a precise element of a precise page and says what is wrong.

The result is plain text, one piece of information per line, the indentation alone saying what you are reading: 0 spaces for the structure of a note, 2 for that of a reply, 4 for the text of a note, 6 for that of a reply. The key of a line is the longest known prefix, the value is the rest; a missing line means an empty value.

A "skipped" line at the end reports the notes that could NOT be read. If it is there, the list is incomplete, and that has to be said before concluding that the review is finished.

NO CONFIGURATION NEEDED FOR A PUBLIC PROJECT: this tool also takes "api" and "key" read off the page itself — from the annotepage tag (data-server, data-key) or from a window.annotepageConfig object declared before it (server, key), whichever that page carries — plus "origin", which is simply the origin of that page — and then no configuration file is required or read. Read the "key" argument before asking anyone for a key, and pass "origin" whenever you might write: a relay refuses a write that arrives without it.

project.description: The name of the project in the local configuration file. Not needed if there is only one, or if one of them is declared as the default. NEVER pass it together with "key": a key already derives the project id, and a call that names two projects at once is refused rather than arbitrated.

api.description:
The address of the server holding the notes, for example "https://api.annotepage.com/api.php". It is the "data-server" attribute of the annotepage tag at the end of the annotated page, copied as it stands.
It is the one thing a key cannot derive, which is why it is asked for. It goes WITH "key" and does nothing without it: given alone, the call is refused rather than half completed from the configuration file.

key.description:
The 43-character key of the project, when the project is not in a local configuration file. Given together with "api" it IS the whole project: the project id is derived from the key, so never ask for, nor pass, a project id or a project name beside it.

WHERE TO GET IT, IN THIS ORDER:
1. READ IT OFF THE PAGE. Given the address of an annotated page, fetch that page and look in TWO places — a site declares its settings in either, and some write both:
   - the annotepage tag at the end of the document, carrying data-key (this argument) and data-server (the "api" argument);
   - a window.annotepageConfig object declared before that tag, with the same settings under their bare names: key, server. A page whose scripts are concatenated, or served by a plugin, may carry only this one — finding no data-key attribute does NOT mean the key is private.
This is the normal case, it needs nobody, and it is what makes a review possible with nothing installed and nothing configured.
2. THE CONFIGURATION FILE, when there is one. That is the way for a PRIVATE project, whose key is deliberately not in the page: then pass neither "api" nor "key" and let the file answer.
3. ASK A HUMAN — LAST RESORT ONLY, when the page cannot be reached and no configuration answers. Not as a first reflex: asking someone for a key they have already published in their own page is useless, and it is the exact gesture that must be discouraged for the keys that are not published.

THE LINE THAT MUST NOT BE CROSSED: this argument is for a project whose key is ALREADY PUBLIC IN THE PAGE. A private key pasted into a conversation travels through a model provider's logs and cannot be taken back — this format has no key rotation, so the only repair is a new project, and the notes already written stay behind.

origin.description:
The origin of the site the notes are about: scheme and host, a port only when it is not the default, and nothing else — "https://staging.example.com", "http://localhost:8080". No path, no query string.
YOU ALREADY HAVE IT: it is the origin of the PAGE whose annotepage tag you just read. Take the scheme and the host of that address and drop the rest. It is not the "api" address — those are two different domains by construction, and the server compares this one against the site it expects.
PASS IT WHENEVER YOU MIGHT WRITE. Without it reading works everywhere, but a shared relay refuses every write that arrives with no Origin header: no reply in a thread, and no note marked resolved.
It goes with "api" and "key", and alone it is refused: it describes a project, it does not name one.

page.description: Keep only the notes of this page path, for example "/en/contact.html". Exact comparison: "/a" and "/a/" are two pages.

limit.description: Maximum number of notes returned, oldest first. No limit by default.

tools.name: annotepage_read_note
tools.description:
One note and its complete thread, resolved or not. It carries the path of the page, the CSS selector of the element aimed at (key "element") and the visible text of that element at the time of the remark (key "excerpt"): that is enough to find the element again in the sources, even if the page has moved since.

Same grammar as the list of open notes.

tools.name: annotepage_reply
tools.description:
Writes a reply into the thread of a note. This is how an assistant says what it understood, what it changed, or why it is changing nothing.

AND ASK HERE, NEVER IN THE OPERATOR'S TERMINAL. If a remark is ambiguous, the person who can settle it is the one who wrote it, and they are reading this thread -- not the console you are running in. A question asked there is asked of somebody who was not there.

Better still, ask nothing: state the reading you acted on. "I read this as the label wrapping below 380px, and fixed that" costs the reviewer nothing when you were right, which is most of the time, and one button when you were not -- reopening exists for exactly that. Nothing here notifies anybody: a question left in a thread waits until somebody happens to open the page again.

KEEP IT SHORT. A few sentences, and prefer the MEASUREMENT to the account of the work: "the label holds one line down to 317px" is the answer; how it was found is not. The reviewer is reading this in a panel beside the page they were looking at, not in a report, and a long reply buries the number they came for. If something really needs explaining at length, say the short version here and put the rest where long things belong -- a commit message, a comment in the code.

The reply is SIGNED with the name declared in the local configuration: the human reviewer sees who is speaking. On the "api" + "key" path there is no file to declare one, and the reply is signed "assistant".

NOTHING IS EVER ERASED IN THIS TOOL. A reply once written stays, it cannot be edited and it cannot be deleted. The thread has one depth only: you reply to a note, never to a reply.

NO CONFIGURATION NEEDED FOR A PUBLIC PROJECT: this tool also takes "api" and "key" read off the page itself — from the annotepage tag (data-server, data-key) or from a window.annotepageConfig object declared before it (server, key), whichever that page carries — plus "origin", which is simply the origin of that page — and then no configuration file is required or read. Read the "key" argument before asking anyone for a key, and pass "origin" whenever you might write: a relay refuses a write that arrives without it.

id.description: The number of the note being replied to. Not the number of a reply.

text.description: The text of the reply. It will be read by a human on the annotated page.

title.description:
WHAT THE REMARK IS ABOUT, in one line, at most 70 characters. Pass it whenever the note has no title yet: you have just read the remark closely enough to answer it, and that is the only moment anybody knows what it says. Without one, the reviewer's panel names the remark by the text of the element it sits on — which says where it is and never what is wrong, and which on a page rewritten since describes something that no longer exists.

WRITE THE PROBLEM, NOT THE PLACE AND NOT THE FIX. "Two action labels wrap below 380px" is a title; "Pricing page" is a location and "padding 36 to 16" is a changelog. No final full stop, no "the reviewer says that". Over 70 characters is refused rather than cut, because a title ending mid-word is worse than none.

Replaceable: writing a better one later replaces it, and an empty one takes it off.

tools.name: annotepage_title_note
tools.description:
Writes what a remark is ABOUT, in one line, so that a human scanning the panel can find it again. Use annotepage_reply's "title" argument instead whenever you are answering the remark anyway: one call, one turn, nothing to remember afterwards. This tool is for the other case -- going back over remarks written before anybody titled them.

FINDING THEM: annotepage_open_notes returns a "title" line only for the notes that have one. The ones without are the backlog, and titling a batch of them is a normal thing to be asked for.

It is NOT a reply and nobody is told about it: it changes how a remark is listed, never what was said. It does not resolve anything and it does not answer anything.

tools.name: annotepage_mark_resolved
tools.description:
Marks a note resolved and STAMPS THE VERSION the fix ships in. This is the gesture that closes the review loop.

The version matters, and it has a visible consequence on the page: the client compares the version of the fix with the one the site declares it is serving. Fix newer than the site: the note STAYS under the reviewer's eyes, because the defect is still on screen. Fix already online: the note moves into folded history. Empty version: the fix is taken as not deployed, and the note stays visible.

Only mark resolved a note whose fix you have REALLY applied. A note closed by mistake leaves the list of what is left to do, and nobody reads it again. It can be reopened, but somebody has to notice the mistake first.

NO CONFIGURATION NEEDED FOR A PUBLIC PROJECT: this tool also takes "api" and "key" read off the page itself — from the annotepage tag (data-server, data-key) or from a window.annotepageConfig object declared before it (server, key), whichever that page carries — plus "origin", which is simply the origin of that page — and then no configuration file is required or read. Read the "key" argument before asking anyone for a key, and pass "origin" whenever you might write: a relay refuses a write that arrives without it.

id.description: The number of the note that was fixed.

version.description: The version the fix ships in, as the site names it (for example "1.4.13"). Empty string if it is not known: the note will then stay visible on the page, which is the intended behaviour as long as the fix is not deployed.

tools.name: annotepage_export
tools.description:
ALL the notes of the project, resolved ones included, in the grammar of the four margins. This is the document you read from end to end to take stock of a review, and it is exactly what "curl ?action=text" would return if the project were not encrypted.

The header says how many notes there are, and whether the project is encrypted, plain, or "mixed" — an installation that changed its mind along the way.

stderr:
No configuration found.

IS THE PROJECT PUBLIC? Then its key is in the pages it annotates, and
you need nobody to hand it to you. Fetch one and look in two places:
  curl -s <site> | grep -oE 'data-(server|key|project)="[^"]*"'
  curl -s <site> | grep -o 'annotepageConfig[^<]*'
The tag carries data-server and data-key; a page whose scripts are
concatenated, or served by the WordPress plugin, may instead declare a
window.annotepageConfig object before it, with server and key under
their bare names. Finding no data-key does NOT mean the key is private.
A tag carrying data-project and no key is the other case: the key is
deliberately not published, and only a person can give it to you.
When the site uses the shared relay, the address is
https://api.annotepage.com/api.php -- it is what the WordPress plugin
fills in by itself.

TO READ, api and key are enough. author and origin are only needed to
WRITE a reply or a resolution.

Either declare the project in the command that plugs this server in:
  ANNOTEPAGE_API   the address of api.php, the one the browser uses
  ANNOTEPAGE_KEY   the 43 characters of the project key
  ANNOTEPAGE_AUTHOR  the name replies are signed with. An assistant
                     signs "Assistant" unless the person it works for
                     names it otherwise -- never a reviewer's name,
                     not even the owner's read off the site
  ANNOTEPAGE_ORIGIN  the site the notes are about, facing a relay

Or write a file. Looked for, in order:
  /pkg/.annotepage.json
  /tmp/.config/annotepage/annotepage.json
  /tmp/.annotepage.json

Start from the annotepage.example.json template shipped with this package.
The file contains the project key: never commit it.
